input.sql: SELECT condition_source_value AS code, COUNT(*) AS n FROM {cdm}.condition_occurrence WHERE condition_concept_id = 0 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC
SELECT c.concept_code, COUNT(*) AS n FROM {vocab}.concept c WHERE c.vocabulary_id = 'ICD10' AND c.concept_code IN ('J18.9', 'J189', 'E11.9', 'E119') GROUP BY 1

input.expression: CASE WHEN d.icd10 ~ '^[A-Z][0-9]{3}$' THEN substr(d.icd10, 1, 3) || '.' || substr(d.icd10, 4) ELSE d.icd10 END
input.rationale: Some ICD-10 codes are recorded without the dot (J189, E119, D649, J069, A150) while the vocabulary stores J18.9 etc.; re-insert the dot after the third character before the lookup.

input.expression: CASE WHEN d.icd10 ~ '^[A-Z][0-9]{3}$' THEN substr(d.icd10, 1, 3) || '.' || substr(d.icd10, 4) ELSE d.icd10 END
input.rationale: Same dot normalisation for the source concept lookup, so condition_source_concept_id points at the ICD-10 concept.

final_text: condition_concept_id was 0 for about 13% of records. Every unmapped code was a valid ICD-10 code written without its dot (J189, J069, D649, E119, A150); the vocabulary stores them as J18.9, J06.9, ... I normalised the code in the lookup expression for both condition_concept_id and condition_source_concept_id. condition_source_value keeps the code exactly as recorded.
